messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-prod GPU queue length > 48k (us-west-2). autoscaler health: degraded. HPA unable to read custom metrics (prom-adapter 502). paging @sarah-oncall

alex: @sarah-oncall getting paged — we have heavy queue growth and multiple customers reporting increased latency/429s. do you have context?

sarah: looking now. I see high enqueue rate to gpu-pool and the HPA metrics target is stale. `kubectl describe hpa inference-gpu-hpa` shows `MetricsUnavailable` for the last 3m.

mike: checking prometheus-adapter logs, looks like adapter is OOMing and restart-looping after a spike in series cardinality from a recent rollout of finer-grained labels on per-route counts. grep from adapter: ```time=\"2026-03-15T14:12:05Z\" level=error msg=\"failed to fetch metrics: 502 Bad Gateway: upstream read timeout\"```

jordan: that matches prom: `prometheus_remote_write`: spikes ~3.5x at 14:09 and scrape latency jumped to 6m. adapter CPU sky-rocketed. this means HPA won't scale, so queue piles up and runtime throttles requests.

ops-bot: Observability snapshot: queue_length(inference-prod) = 48721, throttle_rate = 18.2%, token_latency_p50 = 1.2s, token_latency_p95 = 6.9s. GPU available nodes in pool = 12, pending pod backpressure = 78.

sarah: mitigation plan: 1) manual scale node pool +4 GPUs, 2) temporarily bump replica count for inference dispatcher, 3) reduce prom scrape cardinality (disable per-route granular metric) to stabilize adapter. doing steps 1+2 now. tagging @lina for nodepool ops.

lina: starting manual nodepool resize (aws autoscaling group). command: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name rp-inference-gpu-asg --desired-capacity 16`

deploy-bot: deploy triggered by manual action: scaled deployment/inference-dispatcher from 24 -> 36 replicas by `kubectl scale deployment/inference-dispatcher --replicas=36`

mike: while Lina scales, I can patch prom-adapter to use the fallback query path that avoids high-cardinality labels. patching config: ```kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prom-adapter-config -p '{"data":{"query_override":"/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(inference_requests_total[1m])) by (model)"}}'``` this will reduce label fanout.

alex: note — customers report 429s for batch endpoints, CS notified. @emily-prod please coordinate comms for any affected enterprise customers.

emily-prod: acknowledged, pinged CS and started draft: "We are experiencing increased inference latency and rate-limiting due to GPU autoscaling delays; mitigation in progress, ETA 15-30m."

ops-bot: nodepool resize in progress (ASG activity id: asa-0a1b2c3d). predicted node ready time ~ 7m.

lina: nodes coming up, kubelet registering new nodes: `3/4 nodes ready` -> `4/4 ready` (repeated until all done).

mike: prom-adapter config applied; adapter pods restarted with new query path. logs now show reduced CPU and no 502s for last 45s. ```level=info msg=\"serving metrics requests\"```

ops-bot: HPA metrics endpoint state: available. `kubectl get --raw /apis/custom.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` returns metrics for inference_requests_per_gpu.

sarah: HPA observed increased metric values, started scaling pods up automatically. queue length trending down: 48k -> 29k -> 9k over 10m. throttle_rate -> 4.7%.

jordan: quick root-cause summary in-thread: recent rollout added high-cardinality route labels to per-route request metrics which spiked series count. prom-adapter couldn't keep up and crashed; HPA lost metrics and stayed at old replica/node counts while backlog grew. autoscaler couldn't grow GPU pool quickly enough because it relies on HPA metrics.

alex: customer impact: a subset of enterprise customers on burst traffic saw 429s and latency spikes between 14:08-14:30. no data loss, but degraded availability for short window. CS notified; incident severity = SEV2.

mike: post-mitigation immediate actions: 1) revert per-route labels rollout and roll forward with sampling, 2) add adapter autoscaling / resource guard (CPU/mem limits), 3) add a fallback metric for HPA (queue_length_per_gpu) that HPA can use if adapter unavailable, 4) implement rate-limiter backpressure + graceful deq.

sarah: live handoff: I'm on until 15:00 to watch recovery, then handoff to @jordan-oncall. leaving notes in incident doc and assigning followups.

emily-prod: updated customers: "Mitigation applied, traffic returning to normal. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline for permanent fix."

alex: thanks everyone. immediate indicators look stable. filing postmortem tasks: `/incidents/runs/3723456789/postmortem` and adding owners for the four action items.

ops-bot: auto-note: incident thread closed for active mitigation; monitoring will re-open if queue_length > 20k for >10m. :thumbsup:

jordan: handoff ack. I'll pick up the RCA and coordinate the permanent fixes.
